crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Finding Acquisition Targets
children.blurb: Finding acquisition targets is the front end of private equity and deal sourcing, where a firm turns an investment thesis into a list of companies worth contacting.

children.name: Data Room Diligence
children.blurb: Data room diligence is the review of a target company's documents and records inside a secure virtual data room during a private equity or merger and acquisition process.

children.name: Buyout Modelling
children.blurb: Buyout modelling is the quantitative representation of a leveraged acquisition, covering sources and uses of funds, debt tranches, cash flow sweeps, exit assumptions, and returns such as internal rate of return and multiple of invested capital.

children.name: Private Market Valuation
children.blurb: Private market valuation is the practice of estimating what a private company or a private asset is worth when no public market price exists.

children.name: Tracking Synergies After a Merger
children.blurb: Tracking synergies after a merger means measuring whether the combined company performs better than the standalone businesses would have, across cost, revenue, and capital efficiency.

sections.body: Private equity and deal sourcing is the work of finding companies to buy, checking whether they are worth the price, and then proving the purchase made sense. Artificial intelligence now sits inside each of those steps rather than beside them. Screening tools read filings, registries and news to surface candidate companies that match a fund's stated thesis, and they do it across far more names than an analyst team could read by hand. Inside a data room, models extract figures from contracts, leases and payroll files and flag clauses that carry obligations. Buyout models are built and stress tested with software that links operating assumptions to debt schedules, and after a deal closes, the same systems track whether the promised cost savings actually appear in the accounts.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The screening end is the most mature, because public records and filings are structured enough for machines to parse reliably. Diligence extraction works well on clean digital documents and poorly on scanned, handwritten or inconsistent files, which is still a large share of what sits in real data rooms. Buyout modelling has not been automated in any meaningful sense, since the assumptions that drive a deal are judgement calls about management, competition and timing, and a model cannot supply those. Private valuation remains the weakest area, because comparable transactions are sparse, prices are rarely disclosed, and any automated estimate inherits the bias of whatever sample it was trained on. Synergy tracking is promising but young, and the honest limit is that most claimed synergies are never measured against a clean baseline, so nobody can say with confidence how often the tools get it right.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader should start with Finding Acquisition Targets for the top of the funnel, where screening and sourcing tools do their most visible work. Data Room Diligence covers the middle of the process, the document review that decides whether a deal survives contact with the paperwork. Buyout Modelling explains how the numbers are assembled into a price and a capital structure, and it is the page to read if you want to understand why this step resists automation. Private Market Valuation sits alongside it and deals with the harder question of what a company is worth when there is no public price to check against. Tracking Synergies After a Merger closes the loop, covering the measurement work that happens after the money has changed hands. Together the five pages follow a single deal from first screen to post closing review, and each one can be read on its own if you only care about that stage.
